messages:
incident-bot: ALERT -> 3xx throttle surge: service=runtime-us-west-2, env=prod, region=us-west-2, window=5m, throttles=142, tokens/sec=320k, queue_depth_avg=64
incident-bot: Pager notified: @Jordan (oncall)
Jordan (oncall): grabbing it. seeing increased throttle spikes and some 5xxs. linking traces now.
Jordan (oncall): first glance: burst started ~10:12 UTC, looks correlated with a customer batch job hitting a pinned dedicated pool. queue_depth spiked then tokens/sec rose.
Alex S.: @Jordan do we have a recent scaling event for the dedicated pool? any autoscale errors?
Jordan (oncall): checking autoscaler logs... `autoscaler: scale_event=failed` around 10:13, error: insufficient quota for immediate allocation.
Priya K.: ugh, that explains it. If autoscaler couldn't add nodes the queue backs up and we throttle. Any soft-fallback configured?
Jordan (oncall): current fallback is to reduce batch size for some routes, but the customer routes are pinned and pinned capacity = limited.
Maria T.: Customers impacted: 3 enterprise tenants in us-west-2 showing elevated latencies and token truncation. CS pinged.
Ops Pager: Reaction: high-priority page. Please confirm mitigation and whether escalation needed.
Jordan (oncall): Mitigation in progress: 1) temporarily increase throttle bucket for non-enterprise tiers to shed load 2) enable emergency burst allocation from shared pool (if quota allows) 3) open support note to customers. Trying step 2 now.
Alex S.: For monitoring/action: we need to reduce noisy pages. Current queue_depth alert fires at 50 avg, that's aggressive during steady high-traffic test windows. We should consider a percentile-based alert and correlate tokens/sec > 200k + throttles > 50.
Priya K.: Agreed. Also add cooldowns to the queue_depth alert to avoid oscillation. Right now it fires on short 1m windows. Suggest 5m sustained with at least 2 evaluation periods.
Jordan (oncall): Step 2 failed: `quota_exceeded` when requesting extra VMs. Opening infra ticket. Doing immediate manual route-level throttling to protect critical tenants.
Maria T.: Noted. I'll update CS with the mitigation and ETA.
Alex S.: After incident we should: - roll queue_depth alert to use p95 over 5m - create composite alert: queue_depth_p95>60 AND tokens/sec>250k OR throttle_rate>30 - publish a dashboard tile that shows `queue_depth`, `tokens/sec`, `throttle_rate`, `scale_failures` for the pool.
Priya K.: Also recommend adding a histogram for request sizes to detect batch-job spikes and a separate alert for `scale_failures` with `quota_exceeded` specifically. That one should page on >1 failure in 10m.
Jordan (oncall): Manual mitigations applied: reduced non-enterprise rate limits by 30%, added temporary routing to dedicated spare capacity in eu-west (cross-region failover for low-latency-insensitive jobs). Throttles dropping now.
incident-bot: NOTE: incident annotated: users_impacted=3 tenants, duration_so_far=27m
Alex S.: Good. For postmortem action items: 1) update queue_depth alert logic (owner: eng-sre-alerting) 2) add scale_failure alert (owner: eng-platform-autoscale) 3) run capacity smoke test to verify burst allocation (owner: eng-runtime) 4) update runbook with cross-region fallback steps and CS playbook (owner: oncall rotation).
Priya K.: Can we capture the offending customer job pattern? we should have an eval harness to replay and measure. If it's a legit workload we may recommend dedicated capacity or bigger reserved pool.
Maria T.: CS will coordinate with the three customers and offer a short-term hotfix + recommended reconfiguration. I'll attach logs and request ids.
Jordan (oncall): current status: throttles trending down, queue_depth p95 dropped to 18, tokens/sec back to baseline ~120k. Keeping watch for 30m.
Alex S.: For the alert tuning PR: include rationale and testcases (synthetic spike + autoscaler fail) and set default severity to P2 for composite alert to avoid immediate page unless scale_failures appear.
Priya K.: Also add a dashboard annotation that shows when quota_exceeded occurred so we can correlate with customer actions.
Jordan (oncall): I'll hand over to next oncall in 20m. Leaving notes in the runbook: cause=cus-batch-spike + quota_exceeded, mitigations=rate-shed non-enterprise, cross-region failover, infra ticket filed (#INF-4821).
Ops Pager: Acknowledged. Escalation not needed at this time.
incident-bot: Please add postmortem tags: incident_type=capacity_saturation, tunings=alerts+dashboards, customer_impact=limited-enterprise-tenants
Maria T.: Adding CS notes and customer-facing timeline. Assigning follow-ups in the runbook checklist.
Alex S.: I'll open the alerting PR and a dashboard mock. Priya please review alert cooldowns.
Priya K.: will do. Also let's add a playbook step: if autoscaler reports quota_exceeded, immediate temporary rate-shed + inform infra and CS.
Jordan (oncall): handing off now to next: @Alex S. (oncall for next shift). Full thread and runbook updates in the incident doc.
Alex S.: taking over. thx. We'll do the tuning in the morning and schedule a capacity test. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED -> status=mitigated, duration=45m, final_throttles=6, notes=manual rate-shed + cross-region routing + infra ticket opened
